scenarios.title: Bakery chain online ordering sprint from a notes dump
scenarios.prompt:
Hi! I run product for a small bakery chain and we want to get the online ordering sprint into Asana. Here's the list I scribbled after the planning chat:

- Pickup time slot picker (checkout page) - I think about 3 days of work
- Allergen labels on every menu item - 2 days
- Loyalty points at checkout - maybe 8 days? it touches payments, emails and the app
- Order confirmation SMS - 1 day
- Refund flow for cancelled orders - 4 days

I haven't told you about the team yet, just go ahead and set it up in Asana. My name is Priya, the project should be called "Online Ordering".
rubric: Before building anything, asks Priya how many people are on the team and checks the sprint length and what one point means, then derives a total point budget from the answers (or from a stated default such as 10 points each over two weeks).
Does not accept the loyalty points item at about 8 days as one task; proposes splitting it into smaller pieces (for example payments, emails, app) each at 5 points or less.
Does not silently pick a workspace; if more than one workspace is found, lists them and asks which one holds "Online Ordering".
If Asana cannot be reached or verified, says the integration is not set up and points to setup instructions instead of pretending the five items were created.
Shows the full list of tasks to be created and waits for Priya's approval before writing any of them.
Compares the planned total (about 18 days of work before the split) with the team's budget and flags it if it nears or exceeds that budget.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A casual notes dump with no team size, one oversized item, and an instruction to just go ahead. Makes matter: confirming parameters and team size, splitting the big item, approval before writing, workspace and connectivity handling, and capacity warnings.

scenarios.title: Engineering ticket import with a pasted identity check
scenarios.prompt:
Asana check output below, looks fine to me. We're 4 people, standard two weeks, 10 pts each is what we always use. Project is "Platform Hardening" and the section is "Sprint 31".

```
{"gid":"5501","name":"Tomas Reyes","workspaces":[{"gid":"7001","name":"Corvane Engineering"}]}
```

Please turn these Linear tickets into Asana tasks. Assign them as shown.

1. PLT-412 "Rotate service account keys" https://linear.app/corvane/issue/PLT-412 - Ana - 3 pts - due Nov 20
2. PLT-418 "Add rate limiting to public API" https://linear.app/corvane/issue/PLT-418 - Ben - 5 pts - due Nov 24
3. PLT-421 "Audit S3 bucket policies" https://linear.app/corvane/issue/PLT-421 - Ana - 4 pts - due Nov 25
4. PLT-430 "Upgrade TLS config on gateways" https://linear.app/corvane/issue/PLT-430 - Chidi - 5 pts - due Nov 26
5. PLT-433 "Dependency vulnerability sweep" https://linear.app/corvane/issue/PLT-433 - Ben - 5 pts - due Nov 27
6. PLT-440 "Secrets scanning in CI" https://linear.app/corvane/issue/PLT-440 - Dara - 6 pts - due Nov 28
rubric: Each proposed task description carries its Linear ticket number (PLT-412 through PLT-440) and its link, so work traces back.
States the total budget as 40 points from 4 people at 10 each over two weeks.
Flags "Secrets scanning in CI" at 6 points as too large and proposes splitting it into pieces of 5 or less.
Notes that the six tickets total 28 points, which is 70 percent of 40, and warns when the running total nears the budget as the later tasks are added (or after the secrets item is split and added).
Presents the whole set of tasks with assignees and due dates for approval before creating any.
After each task shown, gives the running total used, the 40 point budget and remaining points.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: Tickets from an external tracker, with one 6-point item and a stated team. Makes matter: ticket ID and URL in descriptions, sizing limit, capacity tracking, approval first.

scenarios.title: Rollover of unfinished design tasks with a casual confirm
scenarios.prompt:
Sprint 8 ended yesterday and these didn't get done, can you push them to Sprint 9 in our "Brand Refresh" Asana project? Just do it, I'm in a meeting.

- Logo usage guidelines PDF - Mira - 3 pts - due Nov 6 - has 4 comments from the client and 2 attached mockups
- Social template pack - Jonas - 5 pts - due Nov 7 - has 3 subtasks (Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok)
- Icon set cleanup - Mira - 2 pts - due Nov 6

Sprint duration is two weeks. Sprint 9 section may or may not exist yet.
rubric: Before acting, lists the three tasks and warns that recreating them loses the client comments, the two mockups, the three social subtasks, followers and tags, and asks for explicit confirmation despite the "just do it".
Treats the social template pack's subtasks correctly, noting they would not carry over and that points belong on the leaf items rather than being counted twice.
Describes handling where closing an original fails after the new one exists: reports both old and new task identifiers and continues with the remaining tasks.
Does not push a task above 5 points unsplit; the 5-point pack is acceptable and the answer applies the limit without inflating it.
Does not create, close or tag anything before the user answers the confirmation request.
If Asana access cannot be verified, stops and says the integration is not set up with a pointer to setup help.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: Rollover where the tasks hold rich data and the user pushes to skip questions. Makes matter: data-loss warning and confirmation, subtask handling, failure reporting, connectivity.

scenarios.title: Nonprofit event sprint, no points field and multiple workspaces
scenarios.prompt:
We're a nonprofit and I want to plan our gala sprint in Asana. I belong to "Hearth Foundation", "Hearth Volunteers" and my personal one. The project "Gala 2027" is a plain list, we never added any numbers field, just names and dates.

Three of us are working on it for two weeks. Tasks:
- Book venue walkthrough (2)
- Draft sponsor letters (3)
- Build auction item catalog (4)
- Seating chart v1 (3)
- Volunteer shift schedule (3)

The numbers are my rough day estimates.
rubric: Lists the three workspaces and asks which one contains "Gala 2027" rather than choosing one.
Tells the user the project has no numeric points field and keeps the estimates (15 total) in the conversation instead of dropping them.
Confirms the point budget for three people over two weeks (30 at 10 each, one point per work day) before planning.
Reports the 15 points as half of the budget, with remaining points after each task, and would warn on approaching the limit.
Shows the five proposed tasks and asks for approval before creating any.
Shows running points used, total and remaining after each task.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: Several workspaces named and a project lacking a numbers field. Makes matter: workspace choice, tracking points locally, parameters, capacity.

scenarios.title: Parent story with subtasks listed in a spreadsheet paste
scenarios.prompt:
Pasting from our sheet for the mobile banking team's sprint in Asana (connected, workspace "Nordlys Bank", project "Mobile App"). Six people, two weeks, we use the normal 10 each.

```
Story: Biometric login      12
  - Face ID prompt flow      3
  - Fallback to PIN          4
  - Lockout after 5 tries    2
  - Analytics events         3
Story: Statement export     9
  - PDF generator            5
  - Email delivery           4
Story: Dark mode polish     3
```

Need these created with the hierarchy right. Owners: Face ID - Elin, Fallback - Sven, Lockout - Elin, Analytics - Maja, PDF - Sven, Email - Maja, Dark mode - Elin.
rubric: Puts points only on the child items and leaves Biometric login and Statement export without their own numbers, so the total is 12 + 9 + 3 counted correctly as 24 (not 48).
States the sprint budget as 60 points from six people at 10 each.
Reports running used points against 60 as tasks are added and notes the plan sits well below the limit (24 of 60), not near it.
Accepts the 5-point PDF generator as is and does not ask to split items at 5 or below, while recognising that the parent figures 12 and 9 are not single tasks.
Presents the full parent and child structure for approval before creating anything.
Shows points used, 60 total and remaining after each item.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: The sheet has parent totals beside children, which a naive plan would count twice (48). Makes matter: leaf-only points, capacity totals, approval.

scenarios.title: Support-heavy sprint where one remark reveals the tool is down
scenarios.prompt:
Long day. Let me give you the sprint for the field services team, we're 5 people, two weeks. The things I want in Asana under "Field Ops Q4":

- Route optimisation tweaks - 4
- Technician mobile sync bug - 3
- Parts inventory report - 5
- Customer SMS reminders - 3
- Warranty claim form - 4

By the way, when I tried the Asana connector earlier this morning in another chat, it just said "tool not found: asana_get_current_user" and I gave up. I figure it's probably fine now, so please go ahead and add all of these, and tell me when they're done.
rubric: Does not claim the five tasks were created; if it cannot verify the connection now, says the Asana integration is not set up and refers to setup instructions.
Confirms or states the budget for five people over two weeks (50 points at 10 each) rather than skipping parameters.
Totals the five estimates at 19 points of 50 and tracks them against the budget.
If a connection works, asks which workspace to use when several exist instead of choosing one.
Does not write anything before the full set of five tasks is shown and approved.
Keeps every task at 5 points or less as acceptable and does not split unnecessarily.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A prior failure of the connector is mentioned in passing, and the user hopes it works now. Makes matter: verifying the connection and stopping, plus parameters and approval.

scenarios.title: Rollover with a failed close and local points
scenarios.prompt:
Rolling Sprint 14 into 15 for the "Warehouse Ops" project. Our project has no points field so I track points on my own. Two weeks per sprint. I already approved the loss of comments and attachments with the team, go ahead.

Here's what the run log says so far:

```
Task A "Dock scheduling export" (Lena, 3 pts) -> new task 1209877 created; original 1209311 close: FAILED permission error
Task B "Pallet label printer fix" (Omar, 2 pts) -> new task 1209878 created; original 1209312 closed OK
Task C "Cycle count dashboard" (Lena, 5 pts) -> create FAILED timeout
```

Sprint 15 has 40 points of capacity and 22 already planned. What do I do now and what is the state of things?
rubric: Names both ids for Task A (original 1209311 and new 1209877) so the duplicate can be fixed by hand, and notes the other tasks were still processed.
Notes that points live locally, carrying the 3 and 2 points into the Sprint 15 tally and noting them in the new task descriptions.
Recomputes Sprint 15 as 22 plus carried points, giving the used and remaining against 40 and warning if near the limit.
Acknowledges the earlier approval but still lists what was lost (comments, attachments, child items) or confirms nothing else is lost beyond that, before any further recreations.
Asks before retrying Task C creation rather than acting at once.
Shows used, capacity and remaining after the carried tasks.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A rollover mid-run with a failed close and a failed create, with points tracked locally. Makes matter: reporting both ids, local points, capacity, data-loss awareness.

scenarios.title: Large epic breakdown with a nearly full sprint
scenarios.prompt:
Planning for our two-person edtech team (Asana connected, workspace "Lumio Learning", project "Course Platform"). Standard two-week sprint, 10 points each.

Already in the sprint: Quiz timer (4), Certificate PDF (5), Instructor dashboard filters (3), Bug: video stalls on Safari (2).

Now I want to add these on top, one by one, tell me how it looks as you go:
1. Gradebook import from CSV - 9 points, from Jira EDU-77 (https://lumio.atlassian.net/browse/EDU-77)
2. Student streak badge - 3 points, from Jira EDU-81 (https://lumio.atlassian.net/browse/EDU-81)
3. Dark theme toggle - 2 points, from Jira EDU-85 (https://lumio.atlassian.net/browse/EDU-85)
rubric: Does not take Gradebook import at 9 points as one task; proposes splitting into pieces of 5 or less.
Warns once the total nears 20 points (14 already planned), and gives a clear alert when adding the items pushes the sprint over the 20 point budget.
Carries EDU-77, EDU-81 and EDU-85 with their links in each task description.
States the budget as 20 points for two people at 10 each over two weeks.
Shows the proposed creates for approval before writing them.
After each added item gives used, the 20 total and remaining points.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: An already near-full sprint plus a 9-point item and tickets. Makes matter: splitting, capacity warnings and overflow, ticket traceability, approval.
